prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Consumer, industrials, financials.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Material company news in retail, restaurants, travel, autos/EV, industrials, defense, space, banks, insurers, gaming — recalls, investor days, guidance, management quotes with numbers.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.

## **BAC** [Financials]
- Bank of America reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of **$29.96 billion** versus the **$30.62 billion** Zacks consensus estimate; shares fell **4.8%** on Oct. 15. The bank also set aside **$1.2 billion** for regulatory fines related to failures to detect potential money laundering (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; Reuters, Oct. 14).[7][10]

## **PGR** [Insurance]
- Progressive reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of **$23.36 billion** versus the **$23.41 billion** Zacks consensus estimate; shares fell **4.2%** on Oct. 15 (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15).[10]

## **PEP** [Retail / Restaurants]
- PepsiCo shares fell **1%** after KFC U.S. announced an exclusive beverage partnership with Coca-Cola, ending PepsiCo’s U.S. relationship with KFC; the report did not provide a contract value or effective date (Yahoo Finance, updated Oct. 16).[9]

## **RKLB** [Space]
- Rocket Lab said the inaugural launch of its larger **Neutron** rocket was delayed until **2027**; shares fell **10.4%** in premarket trading on Oct. 15 (Reuters, Oct. 15).[3]

## **FMC** [Industrials]
- FMC cut its third-quarter outlook and said commercial actions would reduce results by **$625 million–$675 million**; shares fell **42%** in premarket trading on Oct. 15 (Reuters, Oct. 15).[3]

## **NKE / HD / WMT / MCD** [Retail / Restaurants]
- Nike shares rose **6%** on Oct. 15, while Home Depot, Walmart and McDonald’s also advanced during the session; no new company-specific numerical guidance or operating data was reported in the available coverage (Investopedia, Oct. 15).[5]

## **BRK.A / BSP** [Financials / Consumer Internet]
- Berkshire Hathaway announced an additional **$330 million** investment in Bending Spoons; Bending Spoons shares rose **41.2%** and Berkshire shares rose **1.2%** on Oct. 15 (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15).[10]

## Macro [Macro]
- September U.S. retail sales increased **0.8% month over month**, versus the **0.3%** consensus estimate; sales excluding autos rose **0.9%**, versus **0.5%** expected, while the control group increased **0.1%**, versus **0.3%** expected (Investrade, Oct. 15).[4]
- September U.S. producer prices rose **1.3% month over month** and **6.3% year over year**, versus consensus estimates of **0.5%** and **5.3%**, respectively (Investrade, Oct. 15).[4]
- Initial U.S. jobless claims were **199,000** for the latest week, versus **200,000** expected; the four-week moving average was **198,500** (Investrade, Oct. 15).[4]
